text:
maya_support: FYI CS escalated: customer Acme seeing intermittent 502s from Hosted API in eu-west-1 starting ~11:02 UTC. They report streaming responses cutting mid-token and client sees 502. Request IDs: r-1a2b3c4d, r-1a2b3c5e. Attaching their minimal repro curl below.

maya_support: repro curl: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Acme-Meta: <very-long-json>' -d '{"model":"redwood-prod","input":"hello"}'`

sam_eng_sre: thanks @maya_support — do we have edge/ingress logs for those request ids? any 502 from upstream or envoy h2 GOAWAYs?

maya_support: pushing logs now, pasted snippets from edge-proxy for r-1a2b3c4d: `envoy error: upstream reset: connection termination, code: 502, downstream_stream_destroyed`. Also see `upstream reset before response` in nginx access logs.

li_eng_runtime: can you grep for `HTTP/2 stream` and `RST_STREAM` in the envoy logs? long request headers often trigger h2 window/early reset in our chain.

nora_devex: @maya_support did Acme recently enable any metadata header injection? they were testing billing tags last week.

maya_support: yes they enabled `X-Acme-Meta` with huge JSON payload in headers for tracing. They said it works in non-hosted envs but fails at scale on hosted.

sam_eng_sre: that matches a pattern — large headers can overflow nginx proxy buffers or trigger envoy to short-circuit with 502. Also can cause connection pooling to eject upstreams.

li_eng_runtime: quick check: envoy shows repeated `h2_local_goaway` followed by `stream id X: error code: ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` for some sessions. that suggests upstream is getting overwhelmed and sending GOAWAYs.

maya_support: customer timeline: spike at 11:02 after a bulk job that sent 60 req/s with big headers; before that they were fine.

sam_eng_sre: mitigation ideas: 1) ask Acme to revert header injection (short-term) 2) increase nginx `large_client_header_buffers` and `proxy_buffer_size` in frontdoor for eu-west-1 3) add a 502-rate suppress rule to avoid eject loops 4) temp route their traffic to Dedicated to isolate.

nora_devex: we should provide them a small repro curl that trims the header so they can confirm. also recommend chunking metadata into body or use a short id referencing stored blob.

maya_support: sent Acme instructions to disable header injection and gave repro with trimmed header. waiting for confirmation.

deploy-bot: deploy request #PR-4852 rolling config bump to ingress: increase `proxy_buffer_size` to `8k` and `large_client_header_buffers` to `8 16k` for eu-west-1. CI: passed. queued for canary.

sam_eng_sre: good. also adding temporary ingress rule to reject headers > 12k with 400 and log for customer diagnostics — less risky than unlimited buffers.

li_eng_runtime: also patched edge runtime to refuse extremely large metadata headers early (returns 400) — PR merged. will hit canary in 5m.

ops-bot: canary rollout started for ingress-config-euw. nodes: ingress-eu-03, ingress-eu-04.

maya_support: Acme confirms disabling header injection eliminated 502s on their side. they saw no errors after switch.

sam_eng_sre: after canary looks healthy, promote config globally and follow up with postmortem and a doc recommending header size limits.

deploy-bot: ingress-config-euw promoted to region. rollout complete in 12m.

maya_support: marking customer as resolved, will follow up with them about best practices and offer migration path to metadata-by-reference.

nora_devex: follow-ups: docs page for header limits, update quickstarts to discourage big JSON in headers, and notify sales/CS about potential support impact.

li_eng_runtime: retrospective: consider adding a validation layer in frontdoor to turn very large header sets into a metadata payload store + short-id automatically to avoid future user errors.

sam_eng_sre: add incidence tag: edge-502-large-headers, severity: medium, owner: eng-sre.

maya_support: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem is posted. :white_check_mark:
